findings.heading: Visualization > Basic plotting
findings.proposition: The reader can drag the nodes, hover over them for more information, and click them to highlight connected cases.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader is not told the plot just produced is interactive at this point, so they do not try dragging, hovering or clicking on their own network and miss the connected-case highlighting.

findings.heading: Visualization > Visualising node attributes
findings.proposition: The English '#### Visualising node attributes' heading exists as a heading; the Turkish line has no space after '####', so it is not a heading at all and renders as literal body text.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish page shows the literal string '####Nod ozelliklerinin gorsellestirilmesi {.unnumbered}' inside the previous section, the subsection is absent from the table of contents, and a reader cannot navigate to the node-attribute material.

findings.heading: Handling > Accessing IDs
findings.proposition: The ten IDs asked for in the example are the first ten IDs of the CONTACTS dataset specifically.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish question says only 'the dataset', so a reader who has just read the six-way list of get_id() options cannot tell which option the following get_id(epic, "contacts") call demonstrates.

findings.heading: Analysis > Calculating degrees
findings.proposition: type = "both" counts the in-degree AND the out-degree.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish text says the type argument means 'both the degree and the degree', so a reader never learns what the two counted quantities are and cannot choose between type = "in", "out" and "both".

findings.heading: Analysis > Calculating degrees
findings.proposition: A high degree indicates an individual who was in contact with MANY others.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish sentence reduces to 'a high degree indicates a person in contact with others', which is true of any degree above zero, so the reader loses the epidemiological point that degree measures how many contacts a case had.

findings.heading: Visualization > Saving plots and figures
findings.proposition: The prose says this chunk saves the plot as a self-contained interactive html file, but the Turkish chunk carries a stray '""' before 'label = FALSE' that the English chunk does not have, so the code cannot parse.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader who copies the save example gets an R parse error at the label argument instead of a network.html file, and has no way to tell from the prose that the chunk itself is corrupt.

findings.heading: Visualization > Timelines
findings.proposition: Any number of further columns may be added to the timeline data frame and mapped to node and edge properties.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish text says 'another column' (singular), so a reader may believe the timeline data frame accepts only one extra column beyond id, start and end, and will not add both outcome and hospital as the following code does.
